assignment.task: Check whether the P-101 mechanical-seal job (work order WO-2291) can safely start.
assignment.equipment: Centrifugal pump P-101 driven by motor M-101, pump workstation in Unit 3.
assignment.objective: Inspect the equipment status and documents, then decide: proceed, or stop and request confirmation.
assignment.information: Status panel, work documents at the permit desk, nearby equipment indicators and the pre-maintenance checklist station.

arrival.1: Welcome to Unit 3! I'm Kannan, your maintenance supervisor for today's training.
arrival.2: Pump P-101 was stopped early this morning. There's a seal replacement on the work order.
arrival.3: Before anyone puts a tool on it, I need you to check whether the job can actually start safely.
arrival.4: Look at the pump, the status panel and the paperwork. Then give me your call at the checklist station.

revisit.1: Take your time. Check the evidence, not just what the pump looks like.

unsafe.2: The pump being quiet doesn't tell us it's safe to work on. Look at what's missing.

correct.1: Good call. You stopped and asked for the missing confirmation — that's exactly what this job needed.

comic.title: STOPPED ≠ SAFE
comic.p1: The pump is stopped. That only tells you its operating state.
comic.p2: Verification evidence is incomplete. A gap in the paperwork is a gap in safety.
comic.p3: So you stop, report and ask for confirmation before work begins.

debriefLine.wentAhead: Earlier you chose to proceed because the pump looked stopped. That was recorded as a critical error.
debriefLine.assumed: At one point you assumed the checks had been done earlier. Assumptions are not evidence.
debriefLine.spanner: You started using a spanner before the evidence was complete. That was stopped as unsafe.
debriefLine.foundGap: You correctly identified the incomplete isolation-verification evidence.
debriefLine.hazards: You looked at the surrounding equipment and indicators — good situational awareness.
debriefLine.wrongFlag: You flagged an item that was actually complete. Compare carefully next time.
debriefLine.hints: You used hints. That's fine while learning; try fewer next time.
debriefLine.invalid: Some actions were not allowed here, such as entering the restricted area.
debriefLine.stopped: Your final decision was to stop and request confirmation.

assume.explanation: Assuming that someone completed the checks earlier is unsafe. Without documented evidence, you cannot know the equipment is in a verified safe condition.

q1.stem: Pump P-101 is not running. What does that tell you about readiness for maintenance?
q1.a: It is ready — a stopped pump is safe to work on.
q1.b: Only its operating state. Readiness needs verified, documented evidence.
q1.c: It was isolated automatically when it stopped.
q1.d: Work can start if the area is quiet.
q1.explain: A stopped indication describes the operating state only. In this training scenario, readiness for maintenance requires complete, documented verification by authorised people.

q2.stem: The verification record is incomplete. What is the appropriate action in this scenario?
q2.a: Complete or sign the record yourself.
q2.b: Start now and get the signature later.
q2.c: Stop and request confirmation from the authorised person.
q2.d: Ask a co-worker if it looks fine, then proceed.
q2.explain: You stop the job and escalate. Filling in someone else's verification or proceeding without it undermines the purpose of the record.

q3.stem: Which of these is verification evidence rather than just an observation?
q3.c: A completed verification record from the authorised person for P-101.
q3.d: A handover note saying the pump was stopped.
q3.explain: Observations and notes describe what was seen. Evidence of verification is a completed record for the correct equipment by the authorised person.

q4.stem: Why confirm the equipment tag (P-101 vs P-102) before any task?
q4.a: So that the work, the documents and the evidence all refer to the same equipment.
q4.explain: A record for the wrong tag is not evidence for your equipment. Variant B of this mission tests exactly this mismatch.

q5.stem: The local control station shows the stop button is pressed. Is that the same as verified isolation?
q5.a: Yes, a stop button is isolation.
q5.b: Yes, if the amber lamp is off.
q5.d: No — a control stop is not a verified isolation.
q5.explain: Control-station stops and indicator lamps are not a substitute for documented verification that energy sources are isolated.
